svg.text: Pick & Place - BTT Octopus V1.1: what plugs in where
Every connector in use, pin by pin. The letters on the photo match the cards. The Pi side (display, joystick, vacuum sensor) is on wiring.png.
Power in: 8-pole screw terminal, top to bottom
Supply V+ 12 V (logic, HE, fans, fuse F3)
At the input: TVS SMBJ15A + 100 µF across V+ / V− (motor back-EMF on the 12 V rail).
The Pi has its own 5 V / 5 A supply on USB-C. All grounds common.
Motor plug: pin 1 + 2 = coil A, pin 3 + 4 = coil B (1 A1, 2 A2, 3 B2, 4 B1).
Every driver: 1 UART jumper, lower left under the socket. No MS jumpers.
DIAG jumpers: slots 0, 1, 6 and 7 only (bottom right of the board).
MOTOR2_2 stays empty. Set the X2 direction with one belt off, see octopus-fw/README.md.
Find the pins on the TFT header and EXP1 first: see the yellow box. Plugged in reversed, 5 V lands on an input.
Fan voltage jumpers carry the rails directly: a wrong position shorts 5 V / 12 V / VIN.
Octopus USB 5 V power jumper OFF. The board is powered from the 12 V terminal.
All signal pins are 3.3 V logic. DIAG inputs and PA10 are 5 V tolerant; ADC pins (T0-T3, TB) are not.
USB-C to a USB 2 port of the Pi 5: the only link between the two boards.
Shows up on the Pi as /dev/ttyACM0.
X stall, side 1: plug NOTHING in (jumper does it)
X stall, side 2: plug NOTHING in
Z home sensor on the head: 5 V, GND, signal
E-stop button: GND + signal, normally open
On the board: D0-D3 top row, D4-D7 bottom row. A sensor that reads backwards:
SET in_invert_2 / _4 1. Normally closed E-stop: SET in_invert_5 1.
Outputs: screw terminals and fan headers
free (held off; the pump moved to FAN5)
Top camera light, 12 V: jumper on 12 V
free (or a plain 12 V bottom ring instead of NeoPixels)
Head camera fan: always on, cam_fan % (50)
Housing fan (box rear wall): always on, box_fan % (100)
Pi housing fan 30 mm, 12 V: always on, pi_fan % (100)
Vacuum pump 12 V, 400 mA: jumper on VIN, pump_power %
NeoPixel ring DIN (24 LEDs, bottom camera light)
Each fan header has its own voltage jumper (FAN0: 12 V, FAN5: VIN). HE0, HE2, HE3 are held off.
TFT header (5-pin): tool changer board, one data wire
CH32V003 pin 8, TX: the sensor byte
Tool changer board: CH32V003J4M6 (SOP-8), sensor outputs to these pins
Any sensor on any bit: Calibration > Nozzle sensor order learns which bit is which slot.
UART 9600 8N1, one byte 5 times a second, one bit per sensor. Silent for 1 s = sensors not readable, rack moves stop.
To flash the board: unplug the data wire, power it, upload within 3 s. Pin 8 is also the programming pin.
EXP2 and the I2C header are free now: nothing plugs in there.
How to find the pins for certain
1. Nothing plugged into TFT or EXP1. Power the board, set the meter to volts, black lead on any GND screw terminal.
2. TFT header: the pin reading 5 V is pin 5. The pin beside it reading 0 V is pin 4. Two further along is pin 2, the data pin.
3. EXP1: the pin reading 5 V is pin 10, the pin paired with it reading 0 V is pin 9.
4. Pins 1 / 2 are the pair at the far end. Pin 3 (DT) is next to pin 1, pin 4 (SCK) next to pin 2.
5. Once it is wired: set nozzle_count, then Calibration > Nozzle sensor order, and trigger the slots in order.
EXP1: load cell HX711 board (one connector)
3.3 V regulator on the HX711 side: LDO, not a buck (ripple = noise)
HX711 VCC, and its RATE pin (80 samples/s)
MCP1700-3302 or AMS1117-3.3, 1 uF on OUT
Load cell to HX711 (usual wire colours, check yours)
DT and SCK run at its supply,
